definition: Nuance means a slight variation in meaning, tone, or expression.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word nuance. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know nuance should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Chat strips the nuance out of a joke; the wink that saves it in person doesn't survive as a semicolon and a parenthesis.
A distinction goes further than a nuance — it's a difference you can state in one plain sentence, where a nuance is felt before it can be named.
A gulf goes further than a distinction, and much further than a nuance — the difference grown so wide it separates: two positions that no longer share a category, let alone a shade.

A shade is the smallest difference of all — the gap between two blues, borrowed for meanings: a shade of doubt, a shade warmer. It is a nuance wearing its color metaphor, a variation almost too small to state. Nuance is the general word for the same fine difference in tone or meaning.

Subtlety is the fineness itself — of a flavor, a design, an argument — praising how delicately a thing is done, at any scale. A nuance is one particular small difference in meaning, tone, or expression. You admire a translator's subtlety in general; you point at the exact nuance she kept.

When the singer Etta Reyes covered 'Cold Harbor,' she changed no words and kept the original key, yet listeners argued for weeks that the song now meant something different.
Critics reached for the word nuance: the differences were real but small, a matter of tone rather than text.
Reyes let the second verse fall almost to a whisper, and she leaned on the word 'stay' a half-beat longer than the original had.
None of it could be caught in a lyric sheet.
Fans who printed both versions side by side found the pages identical.
The difference lived in delivery — slight turns of voice that listeners felt at once and spent whole message boards trying to phrase.
